title: Decimal Enumeration Skeleton Outline

illustrates.quote: Follow print for the symbol used to represent blanks in a skeleton outline. Insert three dot 5s to represent blank space (no print symbol). A transcriber’s note is required to explain the use of the dot 5s.

blocks.features: Decimal-enumeration skeleton outline; each entry is a decimal number followed by a long blank underscore rule (no text), for the reader to fill in; indentation increases with each additional decimal level.

print.notes: Print’s division numbers are purely decimal (1 / 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.2.1 / 2 / 2.1) — no letters at any level, confirmed directly from the PDF page image (p. 206, printed 8-10).
print.surroundingText: Rule 8.8.5 (Guide Text for Entire Documents in Outline Format) follows on the same/next page.
print.printFeatures: Boxed illustration; each decimal-numbered line followed by a long horizontal underscore rule of blank space, indentation stepping in with each additional decimal level.

braille.notes: Each outline entry ends with the two-character ascii sequence '.-', standing in for the print's long blank underscore — per 8.8.2 this should be exactly three dot-5 cells; margin 8 (this example uses the fixed left margin, not the digit-plus-3 numbered-sample field, since the '1'/'1.1' etc. markers here are the outline numbers themselves, not braille-page line numbers).

resolution: braille.lines byte-identical between A and B. The blank-fill marker ".-" (both runs transcribed it identically but left its dot pattern "uncertain" against rule 8.8.2’s "three dot 5s"): decoded exactly via Emboss’s own canonical BRF-ASCII table (Emboss/engine/brf-ascii.mjs, BRF64) rather than by eye — '.' = dots {4,6}, '-' = dots {3,6}: two ordinary two-dot cells, NOT three dot-5 cells (dot-5 alone is '"' in this same table — compare the literal '"""' guide-dot rows already used in the section-11 precedent, e.g. sample-11-06). This is now a settled finding, not an open uncertainty: the worked example’s own braille does not literally follow rule 8.8.2’s prescription for the blank-fill symbol; kept verbatim as transcribed (not "corrected" to a guessed three-dot-5 rendering). print.notes on the all-decimal numbering (already a Paul decision per the task brief) added from B, confirmed against the same page image.
